Typical Commercial Rebate: Custom: $0.05/kWh (FirstEnergy, +up to $150/kW peak) to $0.15/kWh (PPL), with PECO $0.06-$0.12/kWh and Duquesne $0.08/kWh; FirstEnergy custom capped at 50% of project cost up to $500,000. Prescriptive HVAC examples: PPL tune-ups $60-$125/unit; PECO ~$25-$30/ton for controls/DCV/mini-splits (Phase IV figures).

Instant point-of-sale discounts exist mainly through the Electrical Association of Philadelphia contractor channel in PECO territory.

Commercial Notes: No Michigan utility catalog has a deemed advanced-RTU-controls (compressor-cycling) measure, so HVAC OPTIMIZER rides custom: Consumers explicitly allows automated control technology under custom (calc-based, metering at program discretion; 7-day pre/post line-side metering is the stated standard for VFD customs and a good proxy for what controls projects face). CryoGenX4 is problematic under both customs: DTE excludes 'simple control modifications not involving capital costs' but an additive should count as capital; expect full engineering scrutiny and possible required pre/post metering. High-efficiency RTU replacement is a classic deemed $/ton measure at both IOUs (DTE HE-2 to HE-6; Consumers HV101). RTU refrigerant-charge-correction tune-up (DTE HE-48, $/ton) is an interesting adjacent deemed measure for refrigerant-side work. Reservation BEFORE removing old equipment is mandatory for all custom work at both utilities - retrofit-first sales motions will forfeit rebates.
Residential Notes: Participating-contractor registration with each IOU is a hard gate - Consumers states non-participating contractor installs are ineligible. MiHER uses registered contractors as well. Compressor-cycling controls and refrigerant additives are not deemed residential measures at either IOU; the residential play is riding HVAC replacement/tune-up rebates.

Equipment rebates at OPPD capped at 50% of material cost; $100k/facility/year.

Commercial Notes: OPPD is the standout: ARC (advanced RTU controllers) is an explicit deemed measure at $135-$207/ton, but only devices expressly listed on the application form / approved vendor list qualify, ARC is one-to-one with the RTU, existing buildings only, and a 3-year RTU service agreement (ASHRAE/ACCA 180) is required - getting HVAC OPTIMIZER onto OPPD's approved ARC list is the critical GTM step, because OPPD's T&C explicitly bars ARC equipment from the custom pathway. CryogenX4 would ride OPPD custom ($500/kW, 5% minimum verified savings, PE/energy study, 3-weeks-of-hot-weather sub-metering or June-Sept bill comparison) or EnergyWise custom/industrial-process; refrigeration projects are an explicitly eligible OPPD custom category. Solar-thermal HVAC assist has no prescriptive slot and would also be custom. OPPD prohibits combining custom and prescriptive rebates on the same building in the same calendar year.
Residential Notes: OPPD requires application within the calendar year and within 4 months of install; qualifying heat pumps also unlock OPPD's lower winter conservation rate (Rate 115). EnergyWise pays contractors a $50 dealer incentive per qualified heat pump install. LES SEP funds are annual, first-come first-served. IRA rebates cannot yet be counted on in Nebraska sales motions.

How We Apply (Commercial): Essentially all commercial rebate activity in Delaware runs through one door: the DNREC EEIF online application portal (implemented by NV5), where the contractor can apply on the customer's behalf; the payee must also register in the State of Delaware eSupplier portal to get paid. Delmarva Power has no commercial prescriptive/custom rebate program of its own in Delaware today.
TRM: Delaware Technical Reference Manual (DNREC EEAC), Version 4.0 October 2024 (Version 5.0 draft July 2025); built on the Mid-Atlantic TRM v9 (NEEP)
Typical Commercial Rebate: Prescriptive HVAC $250-$1,500/ton depending on technology; custom $0.20-$0.30 per first-year kWh, both capped at 60% of efficiency-related project cost and $250,000 per address per year
How We Apply (Residential): Dominant design is Energize Delaware Home Performance with ENERGY STAR: an audit ($50/$25 customer cost) by a program-approved contractor is the gateway, then the contractor recommends and submits measure rebates; not an instant/midstream design. Delaware Electric Cooperative uses mail-in PDF applications; Delmarva's Delaware residential portfolio is mostly behavioral (home energy reports, check-ups).
Typical Residential Rebate: HPwES (eff. 11/1/2024): central AC $650-$1,750; ducted heat pumps $800-$2,200; mini-splits $550-$1,700; smart thermostat $150-$200; capped at 50% of installed cost (75% for income-qualified Assisted track). DEC: $300 heat pump water heater.
IRA HOMES/HEAR Status: NOT launched as of mid-2026. DNREC's Home Energy Rebates page says both HER/HOMES ($2,000-$8,000 per home, savings-modeled) and HEAR ($500-$8,000, low-income electrification) are 'expected to launch once funding is received later this year,' still pending U.S. DOE funding/approval; up to $66M total for Delaware. Application was submitted August 2024 with launch originally expected Q2 2025 - roughly a year behind schedule.

Commercial Notes: EEIF is unusually favorable: custom pre-approval is required but M&V is calculation-based (DNREC calculators, spec sheets, or P.E. stamp) with no stated pre/post metering requirement for non-CHP measures - a genuine opening for HVAC OPTIMIZER (single-tier $0.20/kWh; pairs with EMS/multiple end uses to reach $0.25-$0.30/kWh). CRYOGENX4 has a rare explicit hook: the guidelines state 'AC Tune-Up measures (e.g. refrigerant charge adjustment, coil cleaning, airflow adjustment)' on units >65 kBtu/h may be eligible for the custom pathway, itemized by activity; whether a refrigerant additive qualifies needs a DNREC ruling. Small-unit AC tune-ups (<65 kBtu/h) are prescriptive at $50/unit. Very-high-efficiency RTU replacement is classic deemed ($250/ton AC, $500-$1,000/ton HP, tiered IEER thresholds). No trade-ally network - contractor just needs a Delaware business license, trade license, and $1M CGL insurance. 3-year full warranty required on all granted equipment.
